paras: Technology, infrastructure, network architecture, institutional ownership and business economics.
Postal relays, maritime routes, printing, optical semaphore, mechanical calculators, ledgers and early electrostatics.

blocks.h2: Who developed, funded, owned and operated the systems?
paras: Merchants, shipping firms, banks, postal administrations, governments, scientific societies. These participants had different roles: research sponsorship, equipment supply, network operation, regulation, standardization and service consumption should not be conflated.
Physical transport and human-readable messages; administrative records and accounting precede computers.
Couriers, postal charges, trade commissions, credit and insurance; slow information increased uncertainty.
Trade houses and governments coordinated through correspondence; no single universal network existed.

A shipping merchant depended on paper contracts, couriers and trusted intermediaries. A price change could take weeks to reach a distant market. The operating constraint was transportation time, not CPU or bandwidth.
Administrative authority issued postal rules and maintained routes; private merchants and insurers priced risk. The same institutions created demand for faster signaling.
